findings.text: the inventory claims to be re-grounded per def at main HEAD a928b6be and to number fourteen, but the census's own primitive_concepts flags fifteen functions at that revision: reckon/_backends.py:2071:_write_private_json (json.dumps to an O_EXCL sibling temporary, then os.replace) is missing, having landed in 3a1c0f5c after the census snapshot 056c08e0, so a migration wave dispatched from this list leaves one duplicate behind and the one-implementation-per-concept target is unreachable from it.

the read-back compares observed against the payload this thread wrote, so the other writer's whole payload landing between its write and its read is recorded as "interleaved payload" - the same string a genuine blend would produce - so the guard cannot separate the benign race from the defect it exists to catch, and it reddened 1 of 12 runs at head 4d3b229a (stability-concurrency.log, run 3); the membership check at :71 is the form that separates them.

the fragment names c24a4e3c as the revision the head arm ran at, but the log it cites records revision=4d3b229a (head-arm.log:1), so the citation a reader would check does not match; the code is identical across the two commits, so the 43-passed result itself stands.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against a928b6be; c24a4e3c adds the shared helper, write_json_atomically, optional_number and the test file, and 4d3b229a adds the fragment and the figure, all inside the declared scope.
item_verdicts.done_when: the base and head arms, the red negative control and the four behaviours are measured and logged, but the done_when also asserts "the fourteen atomic-JSON writers ... at main HEAD", which no gate measured and which is false at a928b6be, where the census's own detector flags fifteen.
item_verdicts.goal: the goal is to add the one atomic JSON writer and the one numeric decoder that their duplicated copies will migrate to; reckon/_store.py:399 lands write_json_atomically and reckon/_observations.py:21 lands optional_number, and the envelope writer routes through the same helper at reckon/_store.py:362 rather than copying it.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it names the arms in armed JSON form (baseline_suite at exit 2 with its FAILED id, after_suite at exit 0 with none), the negative-control log with its EXIT= line and FAILED test id, and the writer and decoder inventories, and its after_suite revision matches the head-arm log header.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the two reviewed commits touch exactly the five declared paths and nothing else - reckon/_store.py, reckon/_observations.py, tests/test_one_atomic_writer_and_number_decoder.py, docs/evidence/fragments/a-worker-reuses-before-it-writes/one-atomic-writer-and-one-number-decoder.html and docs/figures/a-worker-reuses-before-it-writes/one-atomic-writer-and-one-number-decoder/writer-attributes.svg.

justifications.durability: tests/test_one_atomic_writer_and_number_decoder.py:37 is proven red by the declared mutation and the fsync and decoder guards at :74 and :99 are independent, but the concurrency guard at :57 faulted on a benign race in 1 of 12 runs at head 4d3b229a.
justifications.evidence: the base and head arms and the red negative control are logged with revisions and FAILED ids, but nothing measured the fourteen-writer clause the done_when asserts and the census's own detector contradicts it at a928b6be.
justifications.fit: write_json_atomically sits beside _write_json_envelope in the same idiom and optional_number matches the private-module style, the change adds no ruff finding, and no changed path or symbol carries a forbidden name.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/_store.py:399 and reckon/_observations.py:21 land both primitives as the goal states, but the migration population the goal's duplicated copies must migrate from omits reckon/_backends.py:2071, so the delivered target set is not the set that exists at the named revision.
justifications.scope_discipline: both commits touch only the declared write paths, with no caller migration, no out-of-scope edit and no unrelated rewrite in the files the node passed through.
